docs.title: course-spec
docs.text:
course-spec is an open format for keeping a complete online course in one directory under version control: the outline, HTML slide decks with narration, translations, quizzes with answer keys, and a record of what has been published. People and AI agents write it by hand; tools check it, record it to video, and import it into a learning platform.

building-web-apis/
  course.json                    the course: title, version, languages, sections
  pronunciations.json            how narration says terms
  published.json                 what tools have published, written by them
  theme/deck.css                 shared deck styles
  sections/
    01-designing-endpoints/
      section.json               the section and its lessons
      deck/index.html            slides with narration; data-lesson starts a lesson
      deck/voiceover/transcript.json   narration in other languages
      quiz.json                  the section's quiz with its answer key

docs.title: Why a format
docs.text:
Course platforms keep a course in their own database, edited through a web form. That works for one author clicking through a UI, but not for a course that is written as code and reviewed in pull requests, written partly by AI agents, recorded to video by tools, or published to more than one place. course-spec keeps the whole course in files, with:

  • Stable IDs for every course, section, lesson, quiz, and question, so learner progress and published videos survive edits.
  • Lessons discovered from decks, so the outline can't drift from the slides.
  • Quizzes as part of the course, in one documented format.
  • Source, build output, and published state kept apart, so a fresh clone knows what is live.
  • A validator whose findings name the file, the place, and the fix.

• videoascode records HTML decks to video; course-spec adopts its deck and transcript conventions.
  • AcademyOS imports course-spec directories, plays their decks with browser speech, and grades their quizzes.

The format is licensed MIT, like the code, schemas, and examples.

docs.title: Writing a Course with an AI Agent
docs.text: course-spec is designed for agents: every file is JSON with a published schema, lessons come from the slides instead of being repeated, and the validator's findings carry a code and a fix an agent can act on.

docs.title: Give the agent these instructions
docs.text:
Put this in the course repository's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md:

## Course format

Courses are course-spec directories (https://github.com/academyosio/course-spec).

- After every change, run `coursespec validate --format json <dir>` and fix
  every error before finishing. Fix warnings unless there is a reason not to.
- Lessons come from the deck: a slide with `data-lesson` starts a lesson,
  and its `data-id` is the lesson ID. Don't list them again in section.json
  except to add details.
- Never change a published lesson ID (a `data-id` with `data-lesson`), a
  quiz ID, or a question ID. To remove a published lesson, keep it in
  section.json with `"retired": true`.
- Narration for the default language goes in each slide's `data-vo`; other
  languages go in deck/voiceover/transcript.json, with each slide entry's
  `id` equal to the slide's data-id.
- Decks load only local files by relative paths. No CDNs or web fonts.
- Every quiz question needs an explanation. Vary where correct options sit,
  or set `shuffleOptions`.
- Raise `version` in course.json when content changes: minor for new or
  rewritten lessons, patch for corrections.
- Never edit published.json; tools write it.

docs.title: Give it the schemas
docs.text: The JSON Schemas tell an agent every property and enum value. Print them with coursespec schema <name>, or point the agent at https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/<name>.schema.json once published there. The schema files are in the repository's schema/ directory.

docs.title: Give it an example
docs.text: The repository's testdata/courses/web-apis uses every feature of version 1: a deck with lessons and a title slide, a text lesson placed after a deck lesson, a translation, pronunciations, a quiz with all three question types, a quiz-only final assessment, and a planned section. An agent that copies its shape rarely needs more than one round of fixes.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
1. The agent writes or edits files.
  2. It runs coursespec validate --format json.
  3. For each finding, it reads code, file, pointer, and fix, and changes that place.
  4. It repeats until there are no errors, then reviews the warnings.

Common first-round findings:

Code Usual cause invalid-json A snake_case or misspelled property lesson-not-in-deck A lesson listed in section.json under a different ID than its slide missing-slide-id Slides written without data-id missing-explanation Quiz questions without explanations unlisted-section A new section directory not added to course.json remote-deck-file A stylesheet or font from a CDN

docs.title: The Course Directory
docs.text:
A course directory is any directory that contains a course.json. It need not be a repository's root, so one repository can hold several courses and share a theme between them:

courses/
  shared/theme/
  intro-course/course.json
  advanced-course/course.json

Every file is JSON with camelCase property names and camelCase enum values. Unknown properties are errors, so a misspelled property is reported rather than ignored. Long text, such as a course description or a text lesson, goes in Markdown files the manifests point to.

docs.title: course.json
docs.text:
{
  "specVersion": "1",
  "id": "building-web-apis",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "title": "Building Web APIs",
  "summary": "Design, build, and operate an HTTP API.",
  "descriptionFile": "description.md",
  "languages": ["en-US", "es-ES"],
  "audience": "Backend developers who have built a web app.",
  "outcomes": ["Design resource-oriented endpoints"],
  "prerequisites": [],
  "access": "open",
  "tags": ["apis", "http"],
  "authors": [{"name": "Jane Author", "url": "https://example.com"}],
  "thumbnail": "assets/thumbnail.png",
  "theme": "../shared/theme",
  "certificate": {"enabled": true, "requires": "allQuizzes", "title": "API Designer"},
  "video": {"provider": "youtube", "visibility": "public"},
  "sections": [
    {"path": "sections/01-designing-endpoints"},
    {"path": "sections/02-handling-errors"},
    {"path": "sections/03-versioning", "released": false, "id": "versioning", "title": "Versioning"}
  ],
  "changes": [
    {"version": "1.2.0", "notes": "Rewrote the pagination lesson.", "retakeQuizzes": ["designing-endpoints-quiz"]}
  ]
}
Property Meaning specVersion Required. "1", or "1.<minor>". A reader refuses a major version it doesn't know id Required. Lowercase kebab-case; never changes once published version Required. Semantic: major for restructuring, minor for new or rewritten lessons, patch for corrections title Required summary One line description / descriptionFile A short Markdown description, or a Markdown file for a long one. Set one, not both languages The languages the course is published in; the first is the default. Absent means en-US audience, outcomes, prerequisites, tags prerequisites lists course IDs access open, invite, or paid authors Names and optional URLs thumbnail An image in the course directory theme A directory of shared deck files inside the same repository; default theme/ certificate enabled; requires is allQuizzes, allLessons, or allLessonsAndQuizzes; title defaults to the course title; template defaults to the platform's video How videos are published: provider (youtube or vimeo), visibility (public, unlisted, private), and per-language playlist titles and descriptionFooter text sections Required. Each section as {"path": …}, in order changes The change log; retakeQuizzes names quizzes whose earlier passes are out of date

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Each entry in sections is an object with the section directory's path. The NN- prefix on directory names is for people browsing the tree; the order comes from this list, and IDs come from the manifests.

Every directory under sections/ must be listed, so a forgotten section can't go unnoticed.

A section listed with "released": false is planned but not published. It carries its own id and title, and its directory may be missing or incomplete, so a course can show its whole outline while it is released a section at a time. A platform shows it as coming soon and issues no certificates while any section is unreleased.

docs.title: section.json
docs.text:
{
  "id": "designing-endpoints",
  "title": "Designing Endpoints",
  "summary": "Resources, methods, and status codes.",
  "source": {"type": "htmlDeck", "path": "deck/index.html"},
  "lessons": [
    {"id": "resources", "objectives": ["Model a domain as resources"], "free": true},
    {"id": "glossary", "type": "text", "title": "Glossary", "content": "text/glossary.md", "after": "resources"}
  ],
  "quiz": "quiz.json"
}
Property Meaning id, title Required. The ID is kebab-case and unique among sections summary One line source Where lessons come from: htmlDeck with a path, or none lessons Details for lessons discovered from the deck, matched by ID, or the lessons themselves for a none source quiz The quiz file; defaults to quiz.json when that exists

marp and video sources are reserved for a later version and reported as not yet supported.

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
With an htmlDeck source, lessons come from the deck: each slide with data-lesson starts one, and its data-id is the lesson's ID. A lessons entry adds details to a discovered lesson by its ID:

Property Meaning id Required. Unique within the course title Overrides the discovered title; required for lessons not in the deck type video (the default with a deck) or text content The Markdown file of a text lesson objectives Learning objectives free A free preview estimatedMinutes Used until a recording gives the real length after Places a text lesson after the lesson with this ID; without it, at the end of the section retired Kept to preserve a published ID; not shown to new learners

An entry that isn't a text lesson and whose ID the deck doesn't contain is an error, unless it's retired. That catches a renamed slide.

docs.title: Quiz-only sections
docs.text:
A section with source.type none, no lessons, and a quiz is a quiz-only section, used for a final assessment. Its questions may point at lessons in any section. Every section needs at least one lesson or a quiz.

{
  "id": "final-assessment",
  "title": "Final Assessment",
  "source": {"type": "none"}
}

docs.title: Other files
docs.text: File Contents description.md The long description, when descriptionFile names it pronunciations.json How narration says terms; see Decks and narration published.json Written by tools; see Published state theme/ Shared deck styles, scripts, fonts, and images sections/*/build/ Generated clips, videos, and captions; belongs in .gitignore

docs.title: Decks and Narration
docs.text: A deck is one HTML page per section holding its slides and their narration. course-spec follows videoascode's conventions, so the same deck is validated by coursespec, recorded to video by vac, and played by platforms such as AcademyOS.

docs.title: Slides
docs.text:
<section class="slide" data-id="title" data-title="Designing Endpoints"
  data-vo="Welcome to designing endpoints. [PAUSE:500]">
  <h1>Designing Endpoints</h1>
</section>
<section class="slide" data-id="resources" data-lesson="Resources"
  data-vo="An API is a set of resources.">
  <h2>Resources</h2>
</section>
<section class="slide" data-id="methods" data-lesson="Methods">
  <h2>Methods</h2>
  <aside class="notes">GET reads a resource. PUT replaces it.</aside>
</section>
  • A slide is an element with class slide and a data-id, unique in the deck. Slides nested inside another slide aren't counted.
  • Narration in the course's default language is the slide's data-vo, or its aside class="notes" element. The deck is the only source for that language.
  • [PAUSE:ms] directives are timing for the recording tool, not spoken text.
  • The deck opens at a slide named by the URL fragment, such as #methods, and moves when the fragment changes.

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
A slide with data-lesson starts a lesson. Its value is the lesson's title; when empty, the slide's data-title or ID is used. The lesson's ID is the slide's data-id, so it must be lowercase kebab-case and must never change once published: learner progress and published videos are keyed by it.

Slides before the first lesson start belong to the first lesson, so a title slide joins it. A deck with no lesson starts is one lesson with the section's ID.

In the example above, title and resources make the lesson resources, and methods is a lesson of its own.

docs.title: Self-contained decks
docs.text:
Every file a deck loads, styles, scripts, fonts, images, and media, is in the course directory or its theme and loaded by a relative path. Players that show decks in a sandboxed frame, and offline playback, block network requests, so a stylesheet from a CDN or a font from a font service fails there.

  • A relative file that doesn't exist is an error.
  • A file loaded from another host is a warning, with the fix to download it into the course or theme.
  • Links a learner clicks (<a href>) aren't loads and may point anywhere.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
Narration in other languages lives next to the deck in deck/voiceover/transcript.json, in the videoascode transcript format:

{
  "version": "1.0",
  "metadata": {"title": "Designing Endpoints", "defaultLanguage": "en-US", "defaultVoice": {"voiceId": "…"}},
  "slides": [
    {"id": "resources", "index": 1, "transcripts": {
      "es-ES": {"segments": [{"text": "Una API es un conjunto de recursos."}]}}},
    {"id": "methods", "index": 2, "transcripts": {
      "es-ES": {"segments": [{"text": "GET lee un recurso."}, {"text": "PUT lo reemplaza."}]}}}
  ]
}
  • Each slide entry carries id, the slide's data-id, and translations are matched by it. Matching by position would attach every later translation to the wrong slide after a slide is added or removed.
  • An older transcript without ids is matched by position, with a warning to add them.
  • A slide id that isn't in the deck is an error: it catches a translation left behind by a renamed or deleted slide.
  • A slide with no narration in one of the course's languages is a warning, because recording tools record a language only when every slide has it.
  • Default-language entries, when present, should match the deck; the deck wins and the validator warns when they differ.
  • metadata, such as the voice, is a recording setting that course-spec doesn't read.

docs.title: Pronunciations
docs.text:
pronunciations.json maps a written term to how narration says it, per language:

{
  "ProductBuildersHQ": {"en-US": "Product Builders H Q"},
  "OAuth": {"en-US": "oh auth"},
  "API": {"en-US": "A P I"}
}

Terms match case-insensitively at word boundaries; where terms overlap, the one with more words, then the longer one, wins. Only what is spoken changes: captions and transcripts keep the written term.

docs.title: Narration warnings
docs.text:
• A slide without narration.
  • A lesson whose narration runs over about 10 minutes, at 150 words per minute: split it with data-lesson.
  • With --strict-narration, characters text-to-speech reads badly: (, ), /, and →. Write them out in words.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
coursespec is a Go command. With Go 1.26 or later:

go install github.com/academyosio/course-spec/cmd/coursespec@latest
coursespec --help

docs.title: Check the example course
docs.text:
The repository includes a complete small course, testdata/courses/web-apis: a deck with two lessons and a text lesson, a Spanish translation, a quiz, a quiz-only final assessment, and a planned section.

git clone https://github.com/academyosio/course-spec
cd course-spec
coursespec validate testdata/courses/web-apis
coursespec lessons testdata/courses/web-apis

testdata/courses/web-apis: 0 errors, 0 warnings

building-web-apis 1.0.0 (Building Web APIs)
  designing-endpoints: Designing Endpoints
    new        resources: Resources (2 slides)
    new        glossary: Glossary (text)
    new        methods: Methods (1 slides)
    new        designing-endpoints-quiz: Designing Endpoints Quiz (quiz, 3 questions)
  final-assessment: Final Assessment
    new        final-assessment-quiz: Final Assessment (quiz, 1 questions)
  versioning: Versioning  [planned]

Every lesson is new because nothing has been published yet.

docs.title: Start your own course
docs.text:
1. Make a directory with a course.json:

    {
  "specVersion": "1",
  "id": "my-first-course",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "title": "My First Course",
  "sections": [{"path": "sections/01-introduction"}]
}

  2. Add the section's sections/01-introduction/section.json:

    {
  "id": "introduction",
  "title": "Introduction",
  "source": {"type": "htmlDeck", "path": "deck/index.html"}
}

  3. Write sections/01-introduction/deck/index.html with slides, each a class="slide" element with a data-id and narration in data-vo. A slide with data-lesson starts a lesson:

    <section class="slide" data-id="welcome" data-lesson="Welcome"
  data-vo="Welcome to my first course.">
  <h1>Welcome</h1>
</section>

  4. Run coursespec validate . and fix what it reports.

Next, read The course directory for every field, or Decks and narration for how lessons come from slides.

docs.title: Using the Go Library
docs.text:
go get github.com/academyosio/course-spec@v0.1.0
Package Purpose github.com/academyosio/course-spec (package coursespec) Types for every file, Load, Find, publish status, and published-state reading and writing github.com/academyosio/course-spec/deck Slides, lessons, transcripts, and content fingerprints from HTML decks github.com/academyosio/course-spec/validate Every check, as findings with a fix github.com/academyosio/course-spec/schema The generated JSON Schemas, embedded

The module's dependencies are small, so platforms can import it: an HTML parser for decks, and the schema generator only at generation time.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
import "github.com/academyosio/course-spec/validate"

findings := validate.Course("courses/building-web-apis", validate.Options{})
errs, warns := validate.Counts(findings)
for _, f := range findings {
    fmt.Println(f.String())
}

Platforms import the same function, so a course checked locally passes the same checks on import.

docs.title: Load
docs.text:
import coursespec "github.com/academyosio/course-spec"

c, err := coursespec.Load("courses/building-web-apis")
if err != nil {
    return err // the first problem; use validate for all of them
}
for _, s := range c.Sections {
    fmt.Println(s.ID(), s.Title(), s.Ref.IsReleased())
    for _, l := range s.Lessons {
        fmt.Println("  ", l.ID, l.Type, len(l.Slides), c.Fingerprint(s, l))
    }
    if s.Quiz != nil {
        fmt.Println("  quiz", s.Quiz.ID, coursespec.QuizFingerprint(s.Quiz))
    }
}

Load resolves lessons from decks with the manifests' details applied, matches translations to slides, and reads quizzes, pronunciations, and published state. Unreleased sections without files load with only their ID and title.

docs.title: Find courses
docs.text: dirs, err := coursespec.Find("courses") // every directory holding a course.json

docs.title: Publish status
docs.text: report := c.Status() // sections, lessons, and quizzes as new, changed, published, retired, or planned

docs.title: Decks on their own
docs.text:
import "github.com/academyosio/course-spec/deck"

d, err := deck.ParseFile("deck/index.html")
for _, l := range d.Lessons("section-id") {
    fmt.Println(l.ID, l.Title, len(l.Slides), l.Words())
}
for _, r := range d.Refs {
    if r.Remote() {
        fmt.Println("loads from another host:", r.URL)
    }
}

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
import "github.com/academyosio/course-spec/schema"

data, err := schema.Get("quiz")

docs.title: Published State and Fingerprints
docs.text:
Source, build output, and published state are kept apart:

  • Source is what authors write: manifests, decks, transcripts, quizzes.
  • Build output (clips, videos, captions) is generated into each section's build/ and not committed.
  • Published state is published.json in the course directory, written by tools after recording, uploading, or importing, and committed, so a fresh clone knows what is live. Authors don't edit it.

docs.title: published.json
docs.text:
{
  "courseVersion": "1.2.0",
  "lessons": {
    "resources": {
      "contentFingerprint": "sha256:…",
      "recordingFingerprint": "3f9a1c0b7d2e4a65",
      "durationMs": 151000,
      "videos": {"en-US": {"provider": "youtube", "id": "dQw4w9WgXcQ"}},
      "captions": {"en-US": {"provider": "youtube"}}
    }
  },
  "quizzes": {
    "designing-endpoints-quiz": {"fingerprint": "sha256:…"}
  },
  "video": {
    "playlists": {"en-US": {"provider": "youtube", "id": "PL…"}}
  },
  "platforms": {
    "academyos": {
      "baseUrl": "https://app.academyos.io",
      "courseId": "…",
      "lessons": {"resources": "…"},
      "quizzes": {"designing-endpoints-quiz": "…"},
      "revision": 4
    }
  }
}
  • Keys are course-spec IDs; platform IDs are values, so one course can be published to several platforms.
  • A platform's revision is its revision of the course when this copy was last synced, so the platform can refuse a push from a stale copy.
  • recordingFingerprint belongs to the recording tool, in whatever form it uses; course-spec doesn't interpret it.
  • No secrets, tokens, or private URLs belong in this file.

docs.title: Content fingerprints
docs.text:
A lesson's content fingerprint, written sha256:<hex>, covers everything an author writes and nothing a recording tool chooses. For each of the lesson's slides, in order, it hashes:

  1. the slide's HTML, without the slide element's own data-id;
  2. for each language in the course's languages, sorted by code, the slide's narration: from the deck for the default language, from the transcript for the others, with segments joined by single spaces.

Narration is normalized first: [PAUSE:ms] directives are removed and runs of whitespace become one space. Each value is written with its length before it, so boundaries can't shift.

What follows from that:

  • Splitting the same sentences differently isn't a change.
  • Renaming a slide isn't a change, so a renamed lesson keeps its fingerprint, and the validator can say which new ID it was likely renamed to.
  • The voice, pronunciations, timing, and resolution aren't part of it; they belong in the recording tool's own fingerprint.
  • Theme files aren't part of it, so a theme change marks no lesson as changed. Re-record affected lessons after changing a theme.

A quiz's fingerprint hashes its settings and questions.

docs.title: What the fingerprints tell you
docs.text:
coursespec lessons compares each lesson and quiz with published.json:

Status Meaning new Never published changed Its content differs from what was published published Unchanged since it was published retired Kept for its published ID planned In an unreleased section

coursespec validate uses them too:

  • A published ID that no longer exists is an error, naming the likely rename when a new lesson has the old fingerprint. Restore the ID, or keep the lesson with "retired": true.
  • Content that changed while version still equals the published courseVersion is a warning to raise the version.

docs.title: Writing it from a tool
docs.text:
Go tools write the file with coursespec.WritePublished, which writes the indented form that's committed:

pub, err := coursespec.ReadPublished("course/published.json")
// update pub.Platforms["academyos"], pub.Lessons, …
err = coursespec.WritePublished("course/published.json", pub)

docs.title: Quizzes
docs.text:
A section's quiz, with its answer key, is part of the course, in one format every platform reads. It sits in the section directory as quiz.json, or the file the section's quiz names.

{
  "id": "designing-endpoints-quiz",
  "title": "Designing Endpoints Quiz",
  "passPercentage": 70,
  "allowRetry": true,
  "maxAttempts": 0,
  "showFeedback": true,
  "shuffleOptions": true,
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1-idempotent-methods",
      "type": "multipleChoice",
      "lesson": "methods",
      "prompt": "Which methods are idempotent?",
      "options": [
        {"id": "a", "text": "GET", "correct": true},
        {"id": "b", "text": "POST", "correct": false},
        {"id": "c", "text": "PUT", "correct": true}
      ],
      "explanation": "GET and PUT can be repeated with the same result; POST can't.",
      "points": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "q2-404",
      "type": "trueFalse",
      "prompt": "A 404 means the server failed.",
      "correctAnswer": false,
      "explanation": "404 means the resource wasn't found, a client-side condition."
    },
    {
      "id": "q3-status-code",
      "type": "shortAnswer",
      "prompt": "Which status code means \"Created\"?",
      "acceptedAnswers": ["201", "201 Created"],
      "explanation": "201 Created, with a Location header for the new resource."
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Property Meaning id, title Required. The ID is kebab-case and unique in the course passPercentage 0 to 100 allowRetry Whether a learner may try again maxAttempts 0 means unlimited showFeedback Whether explanations are shown after grading shuffleOptions Asks the platform to shuffle multiple-choice options for each learner; without it, options appear in file order questions At least one

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
Every question has an id unique in the quiz, a type, a prompt, and an explanation. The explanation is required: feedback without a reason doesn't teach. points defaults to 1. lesson, when set, names the lesson the question covers, in any section, so a final assessment can point each question back at what to review.

type Answer key Rules multipleChoice options, each with id, text, and correct At least two options with unique IDs and at least one correct. With more than one correct, the learner must choose exactly the correct set trueFalse correctAnswer, true or false Required shortAnswer acceptedAnswers One or more, compared ignoring case and repeated spaces

A question carrying another type's answer field, such as correctAnswer on a multiple-choice question, is an error, because it is almost always a mistake.

docs.title: Patterns a learner could pass by
docs.text: Without shuffleOptions, the validator warns when three or more single-answer multiple-choice questions all have their correct option in the same position. Vary where the correct option sits, or set shuffleOptions.

docs.title: Final assessments
docs.text: Put a final assessment in a quiz-only section (a none source with no lessons), as The course directory shows. Its questions can name lessons in any section.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text: When a quiz changes enough that earlier passes shouldn't count, list it in course.json's changes[].retakeQuizzes for the new version. Each quiz also has a fingerprint in published.json, so tools notice a changed quiz the way they notice a changed lesson.

docs.title: coursespec validate
docs.text:
coursespec validate <dir>                     # check a course; exits 1 on errors
coursespec validate --format json <dir>       # for tools and agents
coursespec validate --strict-narration <dir>  # also warn about characters TTS reads badly

Given a directory without a course.json, it checks every course beneath it, skipping .git, node_modules, and build directories.

Each finding names its severity, the file relative to the course directory, a JSON pointer or slide, the message, a code, and the fix:

error: sections/01-designing-endpoints/section.json /lessons/2/id: lesson "pagination" is not in the deck [lesson-not-in-deck]
  fix: use the data-id of a slide with data-lesson, or set "type": "text" for a text lesson
testdata/courses/web-apis: 1 errors, 0 warnings

Errors make a course invalid and the command exit non-zero. Warnings point at things that are probably wrong or will hurt learners, such as unnarrated slides or an answer key a learner could pass by pattern.

The JSON output lists each course with its counts and findings:

  "courses": [
    {
      "dir": "testdata/courses/web-apis",
      "errors": 1,
      "warnings": 0,
      "findings": [
        {
          "severity": "error",
          "code": "lesson-not-in-deck",
          "file": "sections/01-designing-endpoints/section.json",
          "pointer": "/lessons/2/id",
          "message": "lesson \"pagination\" is not in the deck",
          "fix": "use the data-id of a slide with data-lesson, or set \"type\": \"text\" for a text lesson"
        }

    }

}

Every code is listed in Validation findings.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
1. Every manifest decodes, with no unknown properties.
  2. IDs: course, section, lesson, and quiz IDs are lowercase kebab-case; lesson IDs are unique in the course, question IDs in their quiz.
  3. Every listed section has a manifest, unless unreleased; every directory under sections/ is listed; every section has a lesson or a quiz.
  4. Each deck exists and parses, its slides have unique data-ids, every lessons[] ID that isn't a text lesson is in the deck, and each relative file the deck loads exists.
  5. Quiz rules from Quizzes.
  6. Every ID in published.json still exists or is retired.
  7. Content changed without a version bump.
  8. Referenced files exist, and the theme stays inside the repository.
  9. Transcripts: every slide id is in the deck, and every slide has narration in each of the course's languages.

coursespec lessons <dir>
coursespec lessons --format json <dir>

Lists each section, lesson, and quiz with its status from published state: new, changed, published, retired, or planned. It needs a course that loads, so run validate first when it reports a problem.

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
Each course-spec file has a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), generated from the Go types, which are the source of truth. Unknown properties are not allowed.

File Schema $id course.json schema/course.schema.json https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/course.schema.json section.json schema/section.schema.json https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/section.schema.json quiz.json schema/quiz.schema.json https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/quiz.schema.json published.json schema/published.schema.json https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/published.schema.json

The schemas check each file's shape. Rules that span files, such as a lesson named in section.json existing in the deck, or a question's lesson existing in the course, are checked by coursespec validate, which also applies every schema rule.

docs.title: v0.1.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-27

The first release of course-spec: an open format for keeping a complete online course in one directory under version control, with Go types, a loader, generated JSON Schemas, and the coursespec command that checks a course and reports what changed since it was published.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One directory per course: course.json, a section.json per section, HTML decks with narration, translations, pronunciations, quizzes with answer keys, and published state, all JSON with camelCase properties
  • Lessons discovered from decks: a slide with data-lesson starts a lesson and its data-id is the lesson's stable ID, in videoascode's deck conventions
  • coursespec validate: every problem with its file, location, code, and fix, as text or JSON, for one course or every course beneath a directory
  • Content fingerprints: each lesson's slides and narration in every language hashed, so coursespec lessons reports what changed since it was published, even in a fresh clone
  • Quizzes in the course: multiple-choice, true/false, and short-answer questions with explanations, checked for answer patterns a learner could pass by

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Go types for the course and section manifests, lessons, quizzes, pronunciations, and published state, with strict decoding that rejects unknown properties
  • coursespec.Load, which resolves a course directory into one value: sections, lessons discovered from decks with manifest details applied, translations matched to slides, quizzes, pronunciations, and published state
  • coursespec.Find, listing every course beneath a directory
  • Planned sections ("released": false) that a course can list before their files exist
  • Quiz-only sections for final assessments
  • Text lessons placed among deck lessons with after, and retired lessons that keep a published ID
  • The deck package: slides, lessons, narration with [PAUSE:ms] directives, the files a deck loads, transcript matching by slide ID or position, and content fingerprints
  • The validate package: schema, ID, section, deck, transcript, quiz, change-log, and published-state checks, with warnings for unnarrated slides, long lessons, remote deck files, missing translations, answer patterns, and unversioned changes
  • Publish status for each lesson and quiz: new, changed, published, retired, or planned
  • coursespec.WritePublished and a platform revision in published state
  • Generated, embedded, and linted JSON Schemas for course.json, section.json, quiz.json, and published.json
  • The coursespec command: validate, lessons, and schema, with --format json
  • A documentation site with guides for the format, validation, AI agents, and the Go library

docs.title: Format decisions in this release
docs.text:
• Every sections entry is an object with a path, so the schema has no union type
  • The pronunciation file is pronunciations.json
  • A deck loads only local files; remote files are reported
  • Renaming a slide isn't a content change, so a renamed lesson keeps its fingerprint and the validator can name the likely rename

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go install github.com/academyosio/course-spec/cmd/coursespec@v0.1.0
go get github.com/academyosio/course-spec@v0.1.0

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Converting a real multi-section course and folding what it finds back into the format, an example course covering every source type, Marp and video sources, QTI export for quizzes, and practice quizzes.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
Write the spec from the terms already in use, and prove it against a real course before calling it done.

The terms are not new. Course, section, lesson, slide, clip, and chapter are already implemented in videoascode's HTML deck support, and quizzes in the AcademyOS grader. A course built without the spec has used the same conventions: lesson IDs from data-id, one deck per section, one quiz per section in the grader's question format. So the spec starts from those, and a real course is ported to it while the types are written, not after. Every gap the port finds becomes a change to the spec.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Types and loader. Go types for the course, section, quiz, and published-state files; Load(dir) resolves a directory into one value, discovering lessons from HTML decks.
  2. Deck discovery and content fingerprints. The deck package finds slides and lessons and hashes each lesson's slides and narration in every language.
  3. Schema. Generate and embed the JSON Schema; lint it.
  4. Validator and CLI. coursespec validate and coursespec lessons, covering every check and warning in the TRD.

  5. Port a real course. Convert an existing multi-section course with decks and quizzes:

  6. the course manifest and its generated lesson list become a course-spec course.json plus one section.json per section, with lessons discovered from the decks;

  7. each quiz moves into its section as quiz.json, with property names and question types in camelCase;
  8. a theme copied into every deck becomes one shared theme directory;
  9. empty video placeholders are dropped; recording and upload write published.json;

  10. the course's own checker scripts are replaced by coursespec validate.

  11. Example course. A small course in examples/ covering every source type and question type, used by tests and docs.

  12. Docs site. MkDocs: terms, layout, each file's reference, validation errors, and a guide for AI agents writing a course.
  13. Release v0.1.0 once the validator and docs are done, so platforms can depend on a published module; porting a real course follows, and what it finds goes into later minor releases.

docs.title: Dependent Work in Other Projects
docs.text:
Project Change AcademyOS Replace its own course sync format with course-spec: load course directories in GitHub sync, import quizzes, honor shuffleOptions, keep platform IDs stable across syncs, map version and changes to course versions, use the certificate title and template, and write its IDs back to published.json videoascode Import deck from this module for lesson discovery and build its recording fingerprint on the content fingerprint; write each transcript slide's id and match translations by id, falling back to position with a warning for older files; record a whole course from course.json (vac course video <dir> --lessons changed); write build output to each section's build/; write fingerprints, durations, and uploaded videos to published.json; serve the directory holding the course and its theme H5pKit Convert a course-spec quiz to H5P content

The import direction is deliberate: deck depends only on an HTML parser, while videoascode's deck package brings in browser automation. videoascode imports course-spec, never the reverse.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: • License. MIT for the code, schemas, docs, and examples, matching the related tools. One permissive license covers everything, including the schemas embedded in code and the examples authors copy into their courses.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
1. Quiz placement. Quizzes come after a section's lessons, and a final assessment is a quiz-only section. RMI-COURSESPEC-015 remains for an exam that should sit outside the section list, if a course needs one.
  2. QTI export. Worth adding once a platform other than AcademyOS needs the quizzes.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: course-spec is an open format for keeping a complete online course in one directory under version control: the course outline, slide decks with narration, quizzes with answer keys, and a record of what has been published. People and AI agents write it by hand; tools record the videos, check the course, and import it into a learning platform. AcademyOS is the first platform to import it.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Course platforms such as Udemy, Thinkific, and Teachable keep a course in their own database, edited through a web form. That works for one author clicking through a UI, but not for a course that is:

  • written as code, with slides and narration in HTML or Markdown, reviewed in pull requests;
  • written partly by AI agents, which need a documented format they can produce and a validator that tells them what they got wrong;
  • recorded to video by tools such as videoascode, so videos are build outputs, not hand-uploaded files;
  • published to more than one place, or moved between platforms.

Without a shared format, every course repository invents its own manifest and scripts. Typical results:

  • A course manifest is generated once by a script and then drifts from the decks it describes.
  • Quizzes live in a platform-specific request format and are uploaded by hand, because the platform's sync ignores them.
  • Published video IDs are pasted into the manifest next to source content, leaving empty placeholder fields until recording finishes.
  • Each repository has its own checker script that only it runs.

Existing standards don't fill this gap. SCORM, IMS Common Cartridge, IMS QTI, and Open edX OLX are packaging and exchange formats: XML-heavy, generated by authoring tools, and designed to move a finished course between learning management systems. None of them is meant to be written by hand, kept in git, or to treat videos as outputs of a build.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. One directory per course. Everything needed to build and publish a course lives in one directory tree that a platform knows how to consume.
  2. Shared terms. Course, section, lesson, quiz, question, slide, clip, and chapter mean the same thing in the spec, in videoascode, and in AcademyOS.
  3. Written by people and agents. The format is readable and writable without tools, documented with examples, and checked by a validator whose errors say how to fix the problem.
  4. Source, build, and published state kept apart. Source is what authors write. Build output (videos, captions, clips) is generated and not committed. Published state (platform IDs, video IDs, durations, fingerprints) is written by tools and committed, so a fresh checkout knows what is already live.
  5. Quizzes are first-class. Quizzes and their answer keys are part of the course, in the spec's own format, so a platform imports them with the rest of the course.
  6. Stable IDs. Every course, section, lesson, quiz, and question has an ID that does not change once published, because IDs key learner progress, video files, and platform records.
  7. Versioned courses. A course has a version and a change log, so a platform can tell learners what changed and whether to retake a quiz.
  8. Any media source. A lesson's video can come from an HTML deck, a Marp deck, or a finished video file. Authors who don't use videoascode still fit.
  9. Several languages. A course can be narrated and published in more than one language, with translations kept as source next to the deck.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Replacing SCORM, Common Cartridge, or QTI as exchange formats. Export to them may come later.
  • Defining how a platform stores, sells, or grades courses beyond what the course itself declares (pass mark, retakes, certificate rule).
  • Defining slide design or themes. The spec names where theme files live, not what they contain.
  • Uploading video. The course declares how its videos are published (provider, visibility, playlist); uploading is a tool's job, and published state records the result.
  • Programs and learning paths that group several courses, such as a free foundation course followed by paid specializations. prerequisites covers ordering in v1; a program manifest may follow.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: User Needs Course author A layout to follow, examples to copy, and a validator to run before publishing AI agent writing a course A precise schema, unambiguous rules, and validator errors it can act on Recording tool (videoascode) Where each section's deck, narration, and pronunciations are, and where to write build output Platform (AcademyOS) One entry point that yields the whole course, quizzes included, with stable IDs to update rather than recreate records Quiz tools (H5P, QTI) Quiz questions and answer keys in a documented format to convert

docs.title: Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Course A complete program of study, with its own version and optional certificate Section A group of lessons on one topic, usually ending with a quiz. Usually one deck Lesson One unit a learner watches or reads and completes: usually one video (Udemy calls it a lecture) Deck The file the slides and narration are written in Slide One screen of a deck Line One sentence of narration Clip The generated audio for one slide's narration Chapter A timestamp marker inside one video. Not a structural unit Quiz A graded set of questions, attached to a section Question One item in a quiz, with its answer key

docs.title: Course
docs.text:
• A course directory has one course manifest: its ID, version, title, summary, description, languages, audience, learning outcomes, prerequisites, access, authors, tags, thumbnail, certificate (rule, title, template), video publishing settings, change log, and ordered list of sections.
  • A course directory is any directory with a course manifest, so one repository can hold several courses.
  • Course-level shared files have defined places: pronunciations, and a theme that several courses in a repository can share.

docs.title: Section
docs.text:
• A section has its own directory with a section manifest: ID, title, summary, its media source, optional per-lesson details, and an optional quiz.
  • A section is self-contained: its deck, narration in every language, and quiz sit in its directory. Translated narration is committed source.

docs.title: Lesson
docs.text:
• When the media source defines lessons (an HTML deck marks lesson starts), lessons are discovered from it, not repeated in a manifest. The section manifest may add details to a discovered lesson by its ID: learning objectives, free preview, duration estimate.
  • When the source does not define lessons (video files, text), the section manifest lists them.
  • Lesson types: video and text. A section's quiz is presented after its lessons.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
• A quiz has an ID, title, pass percentage, retake rules, whether feedback is shown, and whether options are shuffled.
  • Question types: multiple choice (one or more correct options), true/false, and short answer (a list of accepted answers).
  • Each question has an ID, a prompt, its answer key, an explanation, points, and optionally the lesson it covers, which may be in any section.

docs.title: Published state
docs.text:
• One committed file records, per lesson: the content fingerprint of what was published, the recording tool's fingerprint, duration, the uploaded video per language, and captions. It records a fingerprint per quiz and the video playlists. Per platform, it records the platform's IDs for the course, lessons, and quizzes.
  • The content fingerprint covers only what authors write (slides and narration), so any tool can tell a lesson changed. The recording fingerprint adds the recording settings and is interpreted only by the recording tool.
  • Tools write this file; authors don't edit it.
  • Removing or renaming a published ID is a validation error unless the item is marked retired.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• A coursespec validate <dir> command checks a course directory against the schema and the cross-reference rules, and reports each problem with its file and a fix.
  • Warnings help authors and agents write good courses: answer keys a learner can pass by pattern, slides without narration, overlong lessons, and missing translations.
  • The same checks are a Go library, so platforms validate on import with identical rules.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
• Every file is JSON, which agents write reliably and one schema covers. Long text, such as a course description, goes in Markdown files the manifests point to.
  • Property names and enum values are camelCase.
  • Go types are the source of truth. The JSON Schema is generated from them and published under https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
For v0.1.0, delivered by this repository:

  1. A real multi-section course with decks, translations, and quizzes validates with coursespec validate, which replaces that course's own checker scripts and generated manifest.
  2. After a fresh clone, coursespec lessons reports which lessons and quizzes changed since they were published.
  3. An AI agent given only the spec docs and an example course can write a new section that validates on the first or second try.
  4. The AcademyOS import and the videoascode course recording are specified against this version.

When the dependent work in AcademyOS and videoascode lands:

  1. The same course imports into AcademyOS with its quizzes, with no hand uploads.
  2. Rebuilding and re-syncing it updates the existing platform records instead of creating new ones.

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• SCORM, a runtime and packaging standard for learning content in an LMS.
  • IMS Common Cartridge, a packaging format for exchanging courses between LMSes.
  • IMS QTI, a question and test interchange format. It is a likely future export target for quizzes.
  • Open edX OLX, edX's XML course format, which can be kept in git but is written mostly by edX Studio.
  • videoascode HTML decks, where narration lives on each slide and a slide with data-lesson starts a lesson. The spec adopts these conventions.

docs.title: Review Suggestions: Final Assessments, Practice Quizzes, Partial Release
docs.text: From the PBHQ Academy course authors, after planning certificates for From Launch to Traction: six sections, each ending with a quiz, then a final assessment. Three gaps in the spec, in order of need.

docs.title: 1. A quiz-only section for a final assessment (needed now)
docs.text:
The TRD's Quiz section already expects "a review quiz at the end of a course", whose questions point at lessons in any section. But a quiz belongs to a section, and every section needs a source with lessons, so there is no declared place for a course-level final assessment.

Suggestion: allow a section with source.type none, no lessons, and a quiz. State it in the Section Manifest rules, and make the validator accept it.

{
  "id": "final-assessment",
  "title": "Final Assessment",
  "summary": "Scenario questions across the whole course.",
  "source": {"type": "none"},
  "quiz": "quiz.json"
}

Rules worth adding:

  • A section must have at least one lesson or a quiz.
  • In a quiz-only section, each question may set lesson to a lesson in any section, as the Quiz rules already allow.
  • A platform shows a quiz-only section as one quiz item after the previous section, with no video.

On AcademyOS, a quiz is attached to a lesson, so the import would create a quiz lesson in that section, as course.json does today with "type": "quiz" lessons.

docs.title: 2. Practice quizzes (later)
docs.text:
Some courses want section quizzes as practice, with only the final assessment counting toward the certificate. With unlimited retries and feedback on, a section quiz is a learning aid. Requiring it for the certificate adds little once a final assessment tests the whole course.

Suggestion: one optional quiz field, practice (default false). A practice quiz is shown and graded with feedback, but certificate.requires: allQuizzes (and allLessonsAndQuizzes) counts only quizzes that are not practice. No new requires values are needed.

{"id": "measure-before-you-market-quiz", "practice": true, "passPercentage": 70, "questions": []}

Validator: warn when requires is allQuizzes and every quiz is practice, because then the certificate needs no quiz at all.

AcademyOS today: certificateEligible requires a passed result for every quiz in the course. It would skip quizzes marked practice, and the quiz model would need the flag.

docs.title: 3. Releasing sections before the course is complete (needed at launch)
docs.text:
A course is often published a section at a time. From Launch to Traction will launch with its first sections, and later sections follow as they are written. Some depend on weeks of real data. The manifest lists sections by path, and a missing directory is an error, so a course can't declare its full outline while only part of it exists.

Suggestion: let a course manifest list planned sections that aren't released yet:

"sections": [
  "sections/01-from-launch-to-traction",
  {"path": "sections/02-measure-before-you-market", "released": false}
]
  • An unreleased section needs only an ID and title, and its directory may be missing. Validation skips it apart from ID uniqueness.
  • A platform shows it as "coming soon", without lessons or quiz.
  • While any section is unreleased, a platform issues no certificates, even when certificate.enabled is true, and says on the course page that the certificate becomes available when the course is complete.

Without this, authors either hide the outline until the course is finished or turn certificates on by hand at the right moment. The second is easy to get wrong in both directions.

docs.title: Module
docs.text:
• Module path: github.com/academyosio/course-spec
  • Go package: coursespec at the module root, holding the types and the loader.
  • Subpackages:
Package Purpose coursespec Types for every file, and Load(dir) which resolves a course directory into one Course value validate Schema and cross-reference checks, returning findings with file, path, message, and fix deck Discovers slides and lessons in an HTML deck (data-id, data-lesson, data-vo) and computes each lesson's content fingerprint schema Generated JSON Schema files, embedded with //go:embed cmd/coursespec Cobra CLI: validate, lessons, schema
  • Dependencies are kept small so platforms can import the module: invopop/jsonschema (generation only) and golang.org/x/net/html for deck parsing. Recording tools import deck for lesson discovery, not the other way round, so this module never pulls in browser automation.

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
Every file is JSON with camelCase property names and camelCase enum values. JSON is the one format: agents write it reliably, there is no indentation or implicit typing to get wrong, and one decoder and one schema cover every file. Long text goes in Markdown files that manifests point to, such as descriptionFile and text lessons, rather than in long JSON strings.

The loader reads each file's bytes and decodes them with encoding/json into the Go types, rejecting unknown properties. Decoding is kept in one function so another input syntax could be added later by converting it to JSON first, without changing the types, the schema, or the validator.

docs.title: Directory Layout
docs.text:
<course>/
  course.json               course manifest
  description.md            long course description (optional)
  published.json            published state, written by tools, committed
  pronunciations.json       how narration says terms (optional)
  theme/                    shared deck CSS, JS, fonts (optional; see `theme`)
  assets/                   thumbnail, certificate template, course images (optional)
  sections/
    01-<slug>/
      section.json          section manifest
      deck/index.html       media source: slides with narration
      deck/voiceover/transcript.json   narration in every language (optional, committed)
      quiz.json             quiz with answer key (optional)
      text/*.md             text lessons (optional)
      build/                generated: clips, videos, captions, lessons.json (not committed)

A course directory is any directory that contains a course manifest. It need not be the repository root, so one repository can hold several courses:

courses/
  shared/theme/
  intro-course/course.json
  advanced-course/course.json

Rules:

  • Section directories are listed in the course manifest in order. A directory under sections/ that the manifest doesn't list is an error, so a forgotten section can't go unnoticed.
  • A section listed as not yet released may have no directory; see Course Manifest.
  • The NN- prefix is for people browsing the tree; order comes from the manifest. IDs come from the manifests, not from directory names.
  • build/ holds generated files only and belongs in .gitignore.

docs.title: Course Manifest
docs.text:
{
  "specVersion": "1",
  "id": "building-web-apis",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "title": "Building Web APIs",
  "summary": "Design, build, and operate an HTTP API.",
  "descriptionFile": "description.md",
  "languages": ["en-US", "es-ES"],
  "audience": "Backend developers who have built a web app.",
  "outcomes": [
    "Design resource-oriented endpoints",
    "Return errors clients can act on"
  ],
  "prerequisites": [],
  "access": "open",
  "tags": ["apis", "http"],
  "authors": [{"name": "Jane Author", "url": "https://example.com"}],
  "thumbnail": "assets/thumbnail.png",
  "theme": "../shared/theme",
  "certificate": {
    "enabled": true,
    "requires": "allQuizzes",
    "title": "API Designer",
    "template": "assets/certificate.html"
  },
  "video": {
    "provider": "youtube",
    "visibility": "public",
    "playlist": {
      "en-US": "Building Web APIs",
      "es-ES": "Creación de APIs web"
    },
    "descriptionFooter": {
      "en-US": "Take the full course with quizzes and a certificate: https://example.com/courses/building-web-apis",
      "es-ES": "Haz el curso completo con cuestionarios y certificado: https://example.com/es/courses/building-web-apis"
    }
  },
  "sections": [
    {"path": "sections/01-designing-endpoints"},
    {"path": "sections/02-handling-errors"},
    {"path": "sections/03-versioning", "released": false, "id": "versioning", "title": "Versioning"}
  ],
  "changes": [
    {
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "notes": "Rewrote the pagination lesson.",
      "retakeQuizzes": ["designing-endpoints-quiz"]
    }
  ]
}
  • specVersion is required and selects the schema. A loader refuses a major version it doesn't know.
  • version is semantic: major for restructuring, minor for new or rewritten lessons, patch for corrections.
  • description holds a short Markdown description inline; descriptionFile points to a Markdown file for a long one. Set one, not both.
  • languages lists the languages the course is published in; the first is the default.
  • prerequisites lists course IDs.
  • access is open, invite, or paid.
  • theme is a path to a directory inside the same repository, defaulting to theme/ in the course directory. It lets several courses share one theme without copies.
  • certificate.requires is allQuizzes, allLessons, or allLessonsAndQuizzes. title defaults to the course title; template defaults to the platform's template.
  • video is read by upload tools: provider is youtube or vimeo, and visibility is public, unlisted, or private. playlist and descriptionFooter are keyed by language, because each language gets its own playlist; a language without an entry has no playlist or footer. The spec records how videos are published; uploading is the tool's job.
  • changes[].retakeQuizzes names quizzes whose earlier passes a platform should treat as out of date.
  • sections lists each section as an object with its path. Every entry is an object, so the schema has no union type.
  • A section with "released": false is planned but not published, so a course can show its whole outline while it is released a section at a time. It carries its own id and title, and its directory may be missing or incomplete. Validation checks only that its ID is unique and kebab-case. A platform shows it as coming soon, without lessons or a quiz, and issues no certificates while any section is unreleased, even when certificate.enabled is true.

docs.title: Section Manifest
docs.text:
{
  "id": "designing-endpoints",
  "title": "Designing Endpoints",
  "summary": "Resources, methods, and status codes.",
  "source": {"type": "htmlDeck", "path": "deck/index.html"},
  "lessons": [
    {
      "id": "resources",
      "objectives": ["Model a domain as resources"],
      "free": true
    }
  ],
  "quiz": "quiz.json"
}
  • lessons adds details to discovered lessons by ID, or lists lessons for sources that don't define them.
  • quiz defaults to quiz.json when that file exists.
  • A section has at least one lesson or a quiz. A section with source.type none, no lessons, and a quiz is a quiz-only section, used for a final assessment: its questions may point at lessons in any section, and a platform shows it as one quiz after the previous section. On AcademyOS, where a quiz belongs to a lesson, the import creates one quiz lesson for it.

Sources:

source.type Lessons come from Video comes from htmlDeck Slides with data-lesson; the lesson ID is the starting slide's data-id Recorded from the deck marp Slides marked as lesson starts (convention defined when supported) Recorded from the deck video lessons[], each with file (relative path, not committed) or an already-published video The file none lessons[], text lessons only, or none in a quiz-only section None

marp and video are reserved for Phase 3; until then the validator reports them as not yet supported.

In an htmlDeck section, a lessons[] entry with type text is a text lesson placed after the lesson named by after, or at the end of the section without it.

Lesson fields:

Field Meaning id Required. Unique within the course title Required when not discovered; overrides a discovered title type video (default with a media source) or text content Path to a Markdown file, for text lessons, such as text/glossary.md objectives Learning objectives free Free preview estimatedMinutes Used until a recording gives the real duration after For a text lesson, the ID of the lesson it follows retired Kept to preserve a published ID; not shown to new learners

An entry in lessons[] that isn't a text lesson and whose ID the deck doesn't contain is an error, so a renamed slide is caught.

docs.title: HTML Deck Conventions
docs.text:
The spec adopts the videoascode conventions so the same deck records and validates without changes:

  • A slide is an element with class slide and a data-id, unique in the deck.
  • A slide with data-lesson starts a lesson. The value is the title; when empty, the slide's data-title or ID is used.
  • Slides before the first lesson start belong to the first lesson. A deck with no lesson starts is one lesson, with the section's ID.
  • Narration in the default language comes from the deck: a slide's data-vo, or its aside.notes element. The deck is the only source for that language.
  • The deck opens at the slide named by the URL fragment (#<data-id>).
  • Narration may contain [PAUSE:ms] directives, which are timing for the recording tool and not part of the spoken text.

A deck is self-contained: every file it loads (styles, scripts, fonts, images, media) is in the course directory or its theme, referenced by a relative path. Players that sandbox decks, and offline playback, block network requests, so a stylesheet from a CDN or a web font from a font service fails there. The validator checks that each relative reference resolves and warns about each remote one. Links a learner clicks (<a href>) are not loads and may point anywhere.

Theme files: the deck references the course's theme directory with a relative path, which the validator checks resolves. Recording tools serve the nearest directory that contains both the course and its theme, not just the deck directory, so shared files don't need copying into every deck. This depends on support in the recording tool; see PLAN.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
Translations are in deck/voiceover/transcript.json, in the videoascode transcript format, defined by its JSON Schema (pkg/transcript/transcript.schema.json in videoascode). The file lists slides; each slide has its narration per language; each language has a list of segments, one per sentence. Translations are written by hand, so the file is committed source, not build output. Without it, the deck has only the default language.

  • Each slide entry carries id, equal to the slide's data-id, and translations are matched to slides by id. The entry's index is informational. Matching by position would attach every later translation to the wrong slide after a slide is inserted or deleted, and nothing would report it.
  • A transcript written before slide entries carried id is matched by position, with a warning to add the IDs.
  • Default-language entries in the transcript are generated from the deck. Tools use the deck when the two differ, and the validator warns.
  • Transcript metadata, such as the default voice, is a recording setting. course-spec doesn't read it.

docs.title: Content Fingerprint
docs.text:
deck computes a fingerprint for each lesson, written sha256:<hex>. For each slide in the lesson, in order, it hashes:

  1. the slide's HTML, without the slide element's own data-id, so renaming a slide isn't a content change and a renamed lesson can be recognized by its unchanged fingerprint;
  2. for each language in the course's languages, sorted by code, the slide's narration: from the deck for the default language, from the transcript for the others, with the segment texts joined by single spaces. A language with no narration for the slide contributes empty text.

Narration is normalized before hashing: [PAUSE:ms] directives are removed and runs of whitespace become one space. Each value is written with its length in bytes before it, so field boundaries can't shift between slides.

Joining the segments means splitting the same sentences differently isn't a content change. Transcript metadata is never hashed. The fingerprint covers everything an author writes and nothing a recording tool chooses: the voice, pronunciations, timing, and resolution belong in the recording tool's own fingerprint.

The fingerprint doesn't cover the theme's CSS, JavaScript, fonts, or images, so a theme change doesn't mark any lesson as changed. After changing a theme, re-record the affected lessons by ID, or all of them. A theme fingerprint in published.json can be added if this proves a problem.

docs.title: Pronunciations
docs.text:
pronunciations.json maps a term to how TTS should say it, per language. It uses the videoascode pronunciation map:

{
  "SaaS": {"en-US": "sass"},
  "OAuth": {"en-US": "oh auth"},
  "API": {"en-US": "A P I"}
}

Terms match case-insensitively at word boundaries. Only the TTS input changes; captions keep the written term.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
{
  "id": "designing-endpoints-quiz",
  "title": "Designing Endpoints Quiz",
  "passPercentage": 70,
  "allowRetry": true,
  "maxAttempts": 0,
  "showFeedback": true,
  "shuffleOptions": true,
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1-idempotent-methods",
      "type": "multipleChoice",
      "lesson": "methods",
      "prompt": "Which methods are idempotent?",
      "options": [
        {"id": "a", "text": "GET", "correct": true},
        {"id": "b", "text": "POST", "correct": false},
        {"id": "c", "text": "PUT", "correct": true}
      ],
      "explanation": "GET and PUT can be repeated with the same result; POST can't.",
      "points": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "q2-404",
      "type": "trueFalse",
      "prompt": "A 404 means the server failed.",
      "correctAnswer": false,
      "explanation": "404 means the resource wasn't found, a client-side condition."
    },
    {
      "id": "q3-status-code",
      "type": "shortAnswer",
      "prompt": "Which status code means \"Created\"?",
      "acceptedAnswers": ["201", "201 Created"],
      "explanation": "201 Created, with a Location header for the new resource."
    }
  ]
}
  • Question types are multipleChoice, trueFalse, and shortAnswer. A platform maps them to its own names on import.
  • multipleChoice needs at least two options with unique IDs and at least one correct. With more than one correct, the learner must choose exactly the correct set.
  • trueFalse needs a boolean correctAnswer.
  • shortAnswer needs one or more acceptedAnswers, compared ignoring case and repeated spaces.
  • explanation is required. Feedback without a reason doesn't teach.
  • points defaults to 1. maxAttempts of 0 means unlimited.
  • lesson, when set, must name a lesson in the course. A review quiz at the end of a course can point each question at the lesson it covers, in any section.
  • shuffleOptions (default false) asks the platform to shuffle multiple-choice options for each learner. Without it, options are shown in file order, so the validator warns when correct options keep landing in the same position.

docs.title: Published State
docs.text:
published.json is written by tools after recording, uploading, or syncing. Authors don't edit it.

{
  "courseVersion": "1.2.0",
  "lessons": {
    "resources": {
      "contentFingerprint": "sha256:…",
      "recordingFingerprint": "3f9a1c0b7d2e4a65",
      "durationMs": 151000,
      "videos": {
        "en-US": {"provider": "youtube", "id": "dQw4w9WgXcQ"}
      },
      "captions": {
        "en-US": {"provider": "youtube"}
      }
    }
  },
  "quizzes": {
    "designing-endpoints-quiz": {"fingerprint": "sha256:…"}
  },
  "video": {
    "playlists": {"en-US": {"provider": "youtube", "id": "PL…"}}
  },
  "platforms": {
    "academyos": {
      "baseUrl": "https://app.academyos.io",
      "courseId": "…",
      "lessons": {"resources": "…"},
      "quizzes": {"designing-endpoints-quiz": "…"},
      "revision": 4
    }
  }
}
  • Keys are spec IDs. Platform IDs are values, so one course can be published to several platforms.
  • A platform's revision is its revision of the course when this copy was last synced, so the platform can refuse a push from a stale copy.
  • contentFingerprint is the deck content fingerprint the video was made from. coursespec lessons compares it with the current content to report a lesson as changed, even after a fresh clone when build/ is empty.
  • recordingFingerprint is the recording tool's own fingerprint, an opaque string in whatever format that tool uses. The sha256: form applies only to course-spec's content and quiz fingerprints. When only it differs (a new voice, say), the recording tool reports the lesson as needing a re-record; course-spec doesn't interpret it.
  • quizzes[].fingerprint hashes a quiz's questions and settings, so a changed quiz is noticed the same way.
  • No secrets, tokens, or private URLs belong in this file.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
validate.Course(dir) returns findings. Each finding has a severity (error or warning), the file, a JSON pointer or line, a message, and a fix. The CLI prints them and exits non-zero on any error.

Checks:

  1. Each manifest matches the schema; unknown properties are errors, so typos aren't ignored.
  2. IDs: course, section, lesson, and quiz IDs are lowercase kebab-case. Lesson IDs are unique within the course; question IDs within their quiz.
  3. Every listed section directory exists and has a manifest, except unreleased sections; every directory under sections/ is listed. Every section has a lesson or a quiz.
  4. Each source file exists; each HTML deck parses, its slide IDs are unique, and every lessons[] ID that isn't a text lesson is in the deck. Each relative file a deck loads exists.
  5. Quiz rules from the Quiz section.
  6. Every ID in published.json still exists or is marked retired. A published ID that disappeared is an error naming the likely rename.
  7. When a lesson's content fingerprint or a quiz's fingerprint differs from published.json, and version equals the published courseVersion, warn: content changed without a version bump.
  8. Referenced files (thumbnail, certificate template, text lessons, pronunciations.json, transcripts) exist. theme resolves inside the repository; a path that leaves it is an error.
  9. Transcripts: a slide id that isn't in the deck is an error; it catches a translation left behind by a renamed or deleted slide. A deck slide with no narration in a language listed in languages is a warning, because recording tools record a language only when every slide has it.

Warnings that help authors and agents:

  • Without shuffleOptions, three or more multiple-choice questions in a quiz whose correct options all sit at the same position.
  • A slide with no narration (data-vo or aside.notes).
  • A deck that loads a file from another host, which sandboxed and offline players block.
  • A lesson whose narration runs over about 10 minutes, estimated at 150 words per minute.
  • Narration containing characters TTS reads badly, such as (, ), /, or →. Off by default; enabled with --strict-narration.

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text:
• Generated from the Go types with invopop/jsonschema by a //go:build ignore generator, one file per document: course.schema.json, section.schema.json, quiz.schema.json, published.schema.json.
  • Linted with schemakit lint --property-case camelCase.
  • $id: https://academyos.io/schemas/course-spec/v1/<name>.schema.json.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
coursespec validate <dir>            check a course; non-zero exit on errors
coursespec lessons <dir>             list sections, lessons, quizzes, and publish status
coursespec schema [name]             print an embedded schema

coursespec lessons compares content fingerprints, so it doesn't see theme changes; see Content Fingerprint.

Output is text by default and --format json for tools and agents.

Given a directory without a course manifest, validate and lessons act on every course directory beneath it, skipping .git, node_modules, and build/ directories.

docs.title: AcademyOS Course Sync
docs.text: AcademyOS's GitHub sync currently reads its own snake_case course file, which lists lessons inline and leaves quizzes out. AcademyOS replaces that format with course-spec rather than supporting both: its sync loads a course directory with this module, and the old format is retired. No published course depends on it.
